newsitem.title: USA: U.S foreign crudes quiet amid talk of Cusiana deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S foreign crudes quiet amid talk of Cusiana deal.

text.p: The foreign crude scene in the U.S. Gulf was subdued Tuesday amid talk that the last cargo of Colombian Cusiana crudes in the month of July was moved, traders said.
But confirmation of that deal proved difficult since so many players were off their trading desks attending an industry function in Cleveland, Ohio.
Also the trading dead zone between July and August cargoes continued to hamper liquidity, particularly with regards to Brent and other North Sea grades, traders said.
Still, Total was rumored to have sold its Cusiana cargo for July 31-August 1 loading at $1.28 under September West Texas Intermediate fob to a U.S. major.

That deal, if it turns out to have actually been done, would be pricier than the two cargoes of gasoline-rich Cusiana crude Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol sold Monday to a U.S. East Coast refiner for around $1.35 under September WTI fob.
Elsewhere in Latin America, effects on crude markets of the second bombing in a week of Ecopetrol's pipeline that carries Cano Limon crude were not yet clear.
The line, which carries 200,000 barrels per day of the crude, has been out of service since Sunday due to the blasts.

In other action, Glencore was heard to have moved a partial cargo of 380,000 barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe crude oil for late July loading at Dated Brent +$1.80, but that deal too could not be immediately confirmed.
Overall, traders said buyers were still lurking about possibly interested in closing July deals.
But sellers, for reasons not perfectly clear, were hanging back and not floating many offers.
But some cargoes were on offer, including one Indonesian Widuri from a European trading house for August 12-17 loading.
